simple.meaning: גְּזֵלָה (gᵉzêlâh) is a Hebrew action word meaning “that (he had robbed) (which he took violently away), spoil, violence.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 6 times in Leviticus, Isaiah, Ezekiel, beginning at Leviticus 5:23. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to גְּזֵלָה (H1500) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: גְּזֵלָה (gᵉzêlâh) / H1500 is traced through Leviticus 5:23, Isaiah 3:14, Ezekiel 18:7, Ezekiel 18:12 with source-language evidence and verse context.
